correctness.rationale: Signature of symbol i relative to home i is invariant under feasible adjacent swaps. An explicit left/right sorted canonical representative makes every signature fiber nonempty and connected. The only singleton signatures are all-left/all-right. A distance-two swap crosses at most one intermediate home position; the constructive crossing, including the j=i-1 detour, realizes every coordinate flip of the component signature. Thus quotient is precisely Q_(n-2), giving connectivity for n>=4; n=3 has only two isolated 3-cycles. Independent exhaustive BFS on derangements n=3..7 produced 2,4,8,16,32 components with two isolated vertices and all hypercube quotient edges; not an all-n proof.

value.rationale: The sharp transition from disconnected neighbor swaps to connected two-position swaps, with an exact hypercube quotient and explicit coordinate-changing paths, is a structural reconfiguration theorem on a canonical constrained permutation family. It is independently useful beyond the already known component count.

final_claim: For n>=3, legal adjacent-position swaps among derangements give exactly 2^(n-2) signature components and two isolated vertices; for every n>=4, allowing position distance two connects the space and the adjacency quotient of the former components is Q_(n-2).
limitations: Old sign theorem is covered; no claim for n=3 connectivity, cyclic position wraparound, distances/diameters beyond given nonisometric example.
